definitions: A large, rigid slab of solid rock, generally irregular in shape, that makes up the Earth's outermost layer (the lithosphere).
One of the several large pieces of the Earth's lithosphere that are in constant motion, causing earthquakes, volcanoes, and mountain formation.
examples: The Pacific tectonic plate is the largest.
Movement of tectonic plates causes earthquakes.
Volcanoes often form at tectonic plate boundaries.
